content.value_statement: Startup leaders need hiring plans that match stage, budget, and goals. This skill guides role priorities, compensation ranges, equity planning, and org design.
actual_capabilities: Maps team size and core roles for pre-seed, seed, and Series A stages.
Provides role-by-role hiring guidance for engineering, sales, marketing, product, customer success, and operations.
Summarizes US 2024 compensation ranges by role and level.
Explains equity allocation ranges, option pool sizing, and dilution scenarios.
Outlines reporting structures, manager ratios, hiring velocity, and ramp time.
Provides formulas for fully loaded compensation and headcount budget planning.
limitations: Benchmarks are static and may not reflect current salary or equity markets.
Guidance focuses on early-stage startups from pre-seed through Series A.
It does not replace legal, tax, compensation, or employment advice.
It does not access live salary databases, applicant data, or company systems.

use_cases.title: Build a Seed Hiring Plan
use_cases.description: Prioritize first hires, estimate costs, and sequence roles for a seed-stage company with limited runway.

use_cases.title: Review Compensation Budget
use_cases.description: Estimate fully loaded employee costs and compare role plans against revenue and runway constraints.

use_cases.title: Design Reporting Structure
use_cases.description: Create a practical org structure with manager ratios for a growing Series A startup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hiring Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a seed-stage team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seed-stage hiring plan for a B2B SaaS startup with $1M ARR and 12 months runway. Include roles, sequence, budget, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare FTE and Contractor Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for build versus contract decisions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare full-time and contractor options for a five-person product team. Use stage, core work, budget limits, and ramp time.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Series A Org Chart
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a larger growth-stage team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Series A org chart for a 40-person startup growing from $3M to $8M ARR. Include departments, manager ratios, and hiring order.

prompt_templates.title: Model Equity and Budget Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across compensation, equity, and runway.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze equity allocation, fully loaded compensation, and option pool impact for our next ten hires. Show assumptions and decision criteria.

output_examples.input: Seed SaaS company with $1M ARR, $2M runway budget, and urgent engineering and sales needs.
output_examples.output: A prioritized hiring sequence with an engineering lead, two engineers, first sales hire, estimated fully loaded costs, and timing risks.

output_examples.input: Series A company scaling from 18 to 45 employees over the next year.
output_examples.output: A department plan with engineering, sales, customer success, product, and operations headcount plus reporting structure guidance.

output_examples.input: Founder deciding equity ranges for the first five non-founder hires.
output_examples.output: Suggested equity bands by role and seniority, with option pool considerations and dilution assumptions to review with counsel.

best_practices: Start with company stage, revenue, runway, location, and critical business goals.
Use fully loaded costs when comparing hiring plans against budget.
Add recruiting and ramp time before committing to delivery dates.
anti_patterns: Do not copy salary ranges without checking current market data.
Do not overhire before product, sales, and support needs are clear.
Do not treat equity suggestions as legal or tax advice.

faq.question: Does this skill provide salary benchmarks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes US 2024 salary ranges by role and level, but users should verify current market data.

faq.question: Can it create an org chart?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines reporting structures for pre-seed, seed, and Series A startups.

faq.question: Does it replace a compensation consultant?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and should be reviewed with qualified HR, legal, tax, or compensation specialists.

faq.question: Can it help with equity planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides role-based equity ranges, option pool guidance, and dilution examples for planning discussions.

faq.question: Does it work outside the United States?
faq.answer: Partly. The compensation examples are US-focused, so international teams need local market adjustments.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
